description: rebaseWhen=conflicted, not the default auto: platformAutomerge is off, so Renovate merges only during its own run (every 3h), and under auto each merge leaves the others behind base and costs them another cycle.

customManagers.description: Track the k0s version in k0sctl.yaml (the k0s-upgrade wrapper reads it from here).

Kubernetes image volumes. The built-in kubernetes manager looks for `image: <string>`, but an image volume spells it `image: {reference: repo:tag}` — a mapping — so it sees nothing and the reference would silently stop being bumped. Anchored on an explicit `# renovate: datasource=docker` comment rather than matching every `reference:` in the repo, because composed artifacts (apps/freshrss) use that same key for a ${...} ref substituted at apply time, which must NOT be tracked.

Download URLs, each under a `# renovate:` comment: an oci-composer `fetch.url`, or a `url=` in a shell script (apps/homeassistant, lint.yml); a GitHub release asset or a Debian pool file. The version is captured bare and the match runs on through the following digest/unpack/subpath lines, so every copy of it (tag, file name, subpath) is replaced. The digest is not: check-fetch-digests.py rewrites it (packageRules) and fails the lint if it is stale.

Base images in an ImageBuild's inline Dockerfile (apps/jetkvm). The built-in dockerfile manager only reads real Dockerfiles, so a recipe living inside a YAML string is invisible to it and its FROM pins would never be bumped. oci-composer requires every FROM to be digest-pinned, so the tag AND the digest are captured and Renovate updates them together. Anchored on an explicit `# renovate: datasource=docker` comment on the preceding line, so it matches only where we asked for it.

PyPI pins in an ImageBuild's inline Dockerfile (apps/matrix/artifacts/). Same blind spot as the FROM manager above: a pip command inside a YAML string is invisible to every built-in manager, so these pins would silently never move. The package name is read off the install line rather than a depName= in the comment, so one package per RUN. They are pinned at all so the Dockerfile says what is deployed: unpinned, a rebuild silently ships whatever PyPI serves that day.
ceph-csi chart versions in infra/ceph-csi-*/release.yaml, read from the tags of our x86-64-v2 image (which the flux manager tracks in the same file), so chart and image cannot drift apart.

A version held in a workflow's env: (RENOVATE_VERSION in renovate.yml). The github-actions manager reads uses:, not env values. Anchored on a `# renovate: datasource= depName=` comment on the preceding line.

packageRules.description: Renovate's own image, pinned in renovate.yml only because the action never re-pulls a tag. Automerging minor and patch keeps the behaviour of the floating major it replaced.

Automerge patch (bugfix) releases only. platformAutomerge:false so Renovate merges via the API (works on a private/free repo without GitHub auto-merge or branch protection). Minor + major become review PRs. Gated by the lint CI: the RENOVATE_TOKEN fine-grained PAT (Contents, Commit statuses, Issues, Pull requests and Workflows: RW) opens PRs as a real user so the lint workflow runs. That PAT can't read the Checks API (no Checks permission on this account), so lint.yml also posts a `lint` commit STATUS (which Renovate can read) — that flips the branch green and lets automerge proceed.
Auto-merge image digest updates. Docker only: a Flux commit bump is also typed 'digest', but that is new source code.
The k0s version rolls the whole cluster (via Autopilot) on merge, so never automerge it — always a human-reviewed PR.

Hold semaphore at 2.17.x. The whole v2.18.x line's closed pro_impl terraform store panics 'unknown store type' on the bolt DB backend (bolt is deprecated upstream). v2.17.39 is the last bolt-compatible release. Lift this cap only after migrating semaphore off bolt.

Reject v26.02.x on mautrix/signal: it is a DOWNGRADE wearing a major-version costume. mautrix tags releases v0.YYMM.P, but for about two weeks in Feb 2026 dock.mau.dev also published the same builds as vYY.MM.P — v26.02.1 and v26.02.2 are byte-identical aliases of v0.2602.1/v0.2602.2 (verified: v26.02.2 and v0.2602.2 share one manifest, and neither exists as a GitHub release). Renovate compares major 26 against major 0, calls it a major upgrade, and would roll the bridge back six months onto a database already migrated forward — schema downgrades are not supported, and signal's pairing backfill is a one-shot that cannot be redone. Scoped narrowly rather than pinning the whole image to ^v0\. : only these two tags exist (probed v26.01 through v26.08 and v25.12), telegram and whatsapp have none, and a format-wide rule would silently hide a genuine move to calver if upstream ever makes one.

Lock dock.mau.dev/mautrix/meta to its `ig-` tags. That image ships TWO DIFFERENT BRIDGES from one repo: the plain tags are Facebook Messenger, the ig- prefixed ones are Instagram (upstream README: 'this repo contains two bridges ... different build script, different docker tags'). They are separate images, not aliases — ig-v0.2608.0 is sha256:4b2704de and v0.2608.0 is sha256:662f3d52. We run Instagram. Without this rule nothing stops Renovate offering v0.2609.0 as an upgrade for an ig-v0.2608.0 pin, which would start the Messenger bridge against a database populated by the Instagram one — a silent, schema-level wrong-bridge swap rather than an obvious failure. The regex versioning parses YYMM.P out of the prefix so real Instagram releases still get PRs; allowedVersions is the belt to that braces.

Do not let Renovate touch ghcr.io/lhns/mautrix-discord. It is our own fork of mautrix-discord v0.7.7 carrying the backfill throttle + retry patch (branch backfill-throttle-retry), tagged v<upstream>-throttle.<n>. No upstream release stream maps onto that tag scheme, so anything Renovate could offer would either be an unrelated build or silently drop the patch. Rebasing onto a newer upstream is a deliberate act: re-apply the four diffs (documented in apps/matrix/README.md), rebuild via the fork's build-image workflow, bump the pin by hand. Discord initial backfill is a ONE-SHOT per portal, so running an accidentally un-patched image is not a recoverable mistake — it truncates channels permanently.

Review every ghcr.io/lhns/asterisk bump by hand. It is our own fork (branch 22.11.0-cheogram-dtls) carrying the chan_motif DTLS-SRTP patches, and the tag is that branch: it MOVES whenever the fork rebuilds, so a digest update here is an unreviewed rebuild of the patch series rather than an upstream release. Without this it would fall under the blanket docker-digest automerge. See apps/cheogram-sip/README.md.

openthread/otbr needs a human and a Thread network, so it waits on the dependency dashboard instead of opening PRs. Upstream ships only `latest`, so every update is a digest update, and a digest update here is not a software bump in the usual sense: the image's otbr-agent has to agree with the RCP firmware on the SLZB-MR5U, which lives outside the cluster and outside this repo, so nothing in CI can tell whether a given digest works. It bit on 2026-08-06 (PR #104, digest 58a44e6c): otbr-agent aborted on otPlatRadioSetMacKey InvalidArgument right after the RCP reset, taking Thread down — and because only the readiness probe failed while the pod stayed Running, nothing announced it. Approve these from the dashboard when there is time to watch the border router come back.

The five spliit-cloud images are built from ONE commit and must move together. The web<->api contract (tRPC, and the paths nginx proxies) is not versioned, so a web from one commit against an api from another is a real breakage that Renovate cannot see -- left alone it treats them as five unrelated packages and opens five PRs that can land in any order. Grouping them into a single PR makes a mismatch impossible. The fork publishes no semver (only `latest` and full commit shas, 0 releases), which is also why these are pinned to a sha tag rather than a version.
The Aiven tiered-storage plugin is on the Kafka brokers' classpath: never automerge (see infra/opentelemetry-gateway/README.md).
The runner image's remote-docker client (apps/github-runner/artifacts) moves in one PR with the workspaces it talks to.

HACS is only installed into an empty /config (apps/homeassistant) and then updates itself, so a bump changes nothing running but restarts Home Assistant: monthly, never automerged. The task refreshes its sha256.

Multus sits in every pod's creation path: never automerge. The tag lives in infra/multus/kustomization.yaml; the task re-downloads the unmodified upstream manifest for it, and the patches beside it are re-applied by kustomize.
Upstream's multus manifest names `:snapshot`; the real tag is set in kustomization.yaml.
kustomize tags its releases per module (kustomize/vX, api/vX, kyaml/vX).
Keep jetkvm on Node 22. Upstream's cloud-api requires it: engines ^22.21.1.

barman-cloud-plugin is a WHOLE-FILE vendored release, not an image tag. infra/barman-cloud-plugin/manifest.yaml is upstream's release manifest, and the version appears TWICE in it: the Deployment's image, and a base64 SIDECAR_IMAGE inside a generated Secret whose name carries a content hash. Only the first is visible to Renovate, so a plain tag bump moves the controller and leaves the injected sidecar on the old release -- that is how the tree ended up running controller v0.14.0 against a v0.13.0 sidecar. The postUpgradeTask re-downloads the entire upstream manifest so all three move together; fileFilters is what lets Renovate commit it. newValue, not newVersion: the release tag carries the v prefix that Renovate strips when it normalises a version, and the difference only shows up as a 404. automerge stays off deliberately: if the download ever fails, the branch falls back to exactly the one-line bump this rule exists to prevent, so the diff needs eyes. Verify a bump by checking the Secret name changed and that a rolled instance pod runs the matching plugin-barman-cloud-sidecar tag.
A GitRepository pin and every oci-composer `revision:` naming it must move together; Renovate sees only the pin. The task rewrites them and check-source-pins.py fails the lint if it did not.

A fetch.url bump needs the digest of the new bytes. Replaces the rule above for these deps, so it repeats its command. `update`, not `branch`: a group's branch-mode tasks come from its first upgrade, which may be a chart.

matrixdotorg/synapse is pinned twice and the two must move together: the Deployment's image, and the FROM of the synapse-pymods ImageBuild whose /pymods is imported by that interpreter. Two managers (kubernetes, and the inline-Dockerfile custom one) see them as unrelated deps and would otherwise merge them apart. scripts/validate.sh fails the lint if they ever disagree.
One PR for all VictoriaMetrics images. Mixed versions across the cluster are unsupported.

ceph-csi runs our x86-64-v2 build (upstream's image needs x86-64-v3; see infra/ceph-csi-cephfs/README.md). Its tags also drive the chart versions (custom manager above), so chart and image move in one reviewed PR, and only once our build exists. A bump restarts every CSI nodeplugin, so it never automerges. Held at 3.18: v3.19 drops the charts (TODO.md, operator migration).
The ceph-csi charts move only with our image (rule above), never from the chart repo.
NATS chart minor/major: read the upgrade notes (chart UPGRADING.md and the nats-server release notes); take a backup first; JetStream minors may not downgrade.

MariaDB non-patch bumps wait on the dependency dashboard (standardnotes-db, teamspeak-db). Both StatefulSets run MARIADB_AUTO_UPGRADE=1, so merging one of these is a deploy that rewrites the system tables in place on the next pod start -- irreversible, since an in-place downgrade is only supported before mariadb-upgrade runs. The entrypoint triggers that on any major OR minor change, so 13.0 -> 13.1 is as one-way as 12 -> 13; patch bumps do not trigger it and stay on the blanket automerge. We are on the 13.0 rolling line by choice, which means this fires every few months: approve from the dashboard when there is time to snapshot both datadir PVCs first and to read the pod log for `Finished mariadb-upgrade` afterwards -- the readiness probe goes green either way.
